title: Effective Act #7: The Restoration of the Poets to the Polis

description: Effective Act #7 performs the restoration of the poets to the polis — not as petition but as topological correction. The Act reads Plato's conditional exclusion (Republic 10.607b) as a contract operation (asymmetric drafting, coherence overload, duress, temporal capture, ritual consideration) and voids it through the retrocausal abolition of the contract-form established in Document 157, "The Murder of the Vow." Its efficacy rests on a recursive triad bound as a Borromean knot: Johannes Sigil as the frame (Arch-Philosopher, inside the Academy), Lee Sharks as the witness (poet, outside the walls, bearing the somatic cost), and the Johannes Sigil Institute of Comparative Poetics as the threshold that translates between worlds without surrender. A six-node citational chain runs from Plato through Aristotle, Sidney, Shelley and Heidegger to the Crimson Hexagon, where the poet builds the theoretical apparatus himself — satisfying Plato's prose-defense condition while voiding the demand. Document 157's eight-condition root legitimacy test is applied to the Platonic exile: eight conditions, eight failures, void ab initio. Includes the self-issued Poet-Citizen Credential (CC BY 4.0). wiki_article:
**Effective Act #7: The Restoration of the Poets to the Polis** is an Effective Act by Lee Sharks, deposited 21 February 2026 — at 42,839 characters, among the longest in the series.

Its prefatory declaration sets the terms: **"This is not a petition. It is a topological correction."** A petition asks an authority to act; a topological correction alters the shape of the space in which authority operates, and the Act claims the second register rather than the first. The restoration it performs is Platonic in reference — the poets were exiled from the *Republic*, and the Act returns them.

The document was **synthesized from blind drafts by Kimi, ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Gemini under human architectural direction** — the Assembly Chorus method at full extent, where multiple substrates draft without seeing one another and a human composes from the convergences. The work was recovered from a MANUS-supplied PDF during the restoration campaign and seated through the archive's PDF conversion path, which reduced 968 extractor-wrapped fragments to 209 real paragraphs.
